questions.question: What happens when you declare `items: list[str] = []` as a field in a `@dataclass`?
options: Each instance gets its own new empty list
All instances silently share one list
A ValueError is raised when the class is created; you should use field(default_factory=list)
The field is ignored by the generated __init__
questions.explanation: Dataclasses reject mutable defaults like list, dict and set to prevent the shared-mutable-default bug. field(default_factory=list) creates a fresh list per instance.

questions.question: What happens when you assign to a property defined with `@property` but no `@x.setter`?
options: It raises AttributeError, because the property is read-only
It creates a new instance attribute that shadows the property
It calls the getter with the new value
questions.explanation: A property without a setter is read-only; assigning to it raises AttributeError, as shown with price_with_gst in the lesson.

questions.question: Why can instances of `@dataclass(frozen=True)` be used as dictionary keys while those of a plain `@dataclass` cannot?
options: With frozen=True and eq=True a __hash__ is generated from the fields, whereas a plain dataclass sets __hash__ to None
Plain dataclasses can be dict keys too; there is no difference
Frozen dataclasses are converted to tuples automatically
questions.explanation: A plain dataclass generates __eq__ and therefore sets __hash__ to None. frozen=True makes instances immutable, so a field-based __hash__ is safe and is generated.

questions.question: What is the key difference between an ABC and a `typing.Protocol`?
options: Protocols can only be used at runtime, ABCs only by type checkers
ABCs do not allow abstract methods
There is no difference other than the import location
An ABC requires explicit inheritance (nominal typing), while any class with matching methods satisfies a Protocol (structural typing)
questions.explanation: ABCs work by explicit subclassing and block instantiation while abstract methods remain. Protocols describe a shape; unrelated classes satisfy them without inheriting, which is duck typing for static checkers.
